Préambule: Reprise après interruption. L’état est dans la branche. Commence par établir ce qui est fait et ce qui reste par question (Q1 à Q28), sans refaire ce qui est fait.
Voici le prompt original:
```

<pasted_content id="c845">
Arbitrages (rapport bloquant, section 7) :

Q1 : (b). Ajouter à §63 « la destination est utilisable dans l'état d'arrivée ».
Q2 : lecture mixte sur l'état d'arrivée : invariants du noyau sur l'état entier, plus ArenaInv de la nouvelle entrée ; NewArenaBase porte cette lecture.
Q3 : réalisation par des pas du noyau. freeSlot (contrat HandlePool v0.5) marque l'entrée libre et incrémente la génération ; préconditions : droit d'administration, pool vivant, handle valide, aucune feuille de l'entrée à Init (Uninit ou Moved), aucune autorité active dérivée d'une compagne de ce pool sur l'entrée ; aucun effet d'endUse. Deux preuves obligatoires :
  (1) témoin complet depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés : newPool, allocSlot, resolve Modify, écriture, transfer de la valeur vers un local de même forme, unresolve, freeSlot accepté ;
  (2) la mise à jour des métadonnées (état libre, génération) est réalisable par une écriture autorisée sous le droit d'administration.
Q4 : garantie par pool : réécrire D.2, D.3 et D.4(3) sur les compagnes du pool du slot ; les pools imbriqués restent permis ; I1 et les garanties du noyau restent prouvées sur l'état entier.
Q5 : la validation du handle précède le contrôle du droit : fail dans les deux cas.
Q6 : réécrire §86 s4 : « La réémission ne modifie ni les octets ni l'état d'initialisation. Une lecture reste soumise aux conditions ordinaires du modèle mémoire, notamment Init, aux droits d'accès et à la validité de représentation pour le type demandé. La Spec 4 déterminera les obligations de construction et de typage des valeurs réémises. »
Q7 : restreindre §78.3 aux ancres du sous-arbre strict de internal qui couvrent une feuille du stockage administré ; prouver que la clause découle de §78.2 et de I3 (lecture Q9), et l'équivalence de reset avec sa séquence du noyau dans les deux sens.
Q8 : ajouter à §47 : le graphe de possession des statiques est acyclique.
Q9 et Q26 : « valide » = active. §69.2 : endUse est rejeté si une autorité détenue par place a un descendant actif détenu ailleurs.
Q10 : (a).
Q11 : (a) fail ; (b) reject ; (c) reject ; (d) mark exige AdminRight ; (e) grow suit le détenteur actuel du bloc ; (f) fail avant le contrôle du droit (contrat DS-v2).
Q12 : avec le nouveau freeSlot, un handle d'entrée libre est périmé : fail.
Q13 : §71.2 inchangé ; préciser au §36 que MetaRight vise la création ou le recyclage d'autorités sur un stockage existant, pas la création d'une allocation fraîche par alloc ; la concurrence entre appels relève de la spec 2.
Q14 : « opérations d'accès » = O9–O11 ; le préciser au §59.
Q15 : restreindre §40 aux emplacements racines utilisables, comme §49.7.
Q16 : définir I5 : toute feuille épinglée appartient à un emplacement utilisable.
Q17 : lecture actuelle.
Q18 : région dont toutes les feuilles sont de taille nulle : base et provenance de l'allocation de l'ancre effective, comme la région vide.
Q19 : H31a : le jumeau à plusieurs pas (conjonct 5) est accepté.
Q20 : non bloquants (classés).
Q21 : pour chaque cas dont le verdict attendu change, conserver le verdict historique, sa justification et le nouveau verdict fondé sur la v0.1 (tableau dans la description de PR) :
  - H21, H50, H51 : nouveau verdict = verdict obtenu ;
  - H49 : conservé comme test de régression, verdict = verdict obtenu, blocage résiduel documenté (décision NoLock) ; exception explicite : le reset rejeté de H49 est dispensé de jumeau positif ;
  - H16 classé spec 3 ; W2 et W3 : les variantes deviennent les cas ; MM2-H H01 : la variante devient le jumeau ; H10 : l'accès sort de l'allocation ; W1 : la valeur est retirée avant freeSlot.
Q22 : non bloquants (frontières ouvertes de la spec) ; exitRoots retenu comme réalisation de référence.
Q23 : lectures dont un témoin du rapport change un verdict :
  - B#1, B#15, B#33, SP-A4, machine S1 et S2 : lectures actuelles conservées (B#15 imposée par Q9) ;
  - B#28 : remplacée par Q9 ;
  - B#45 : remplacée : chaque pin crée une obligation d'épinglage d'identité fraîche ; une feuille est épinglée tant qu'une obligation active la couvre ; unpin désigne une obligation et ne lève qu'elle ; K.ExternalDone porte sur cette obligation ;
  - H-R5 : sans objet ; DS-R1 à DS-R13 : tranchées par Q11, Q27 et Q28.
  Les lectures sans témoin de différence sont conservées.
Q24 : le fournisseur doit être un emplacement utilisable (§71.2).
Q25 : (b).
Q27 : (a).
Q28 : (c) fail (une pile morte invalide ses marques).

Spec : ne pas modifier `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`. Créer `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` à partir de la v0, avec les amendements Q1, Q2, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q9/Q26, Q13, Q14, Q15, Q16, Q18, Q24 et B#45 (§74, §75), en anglais ; en-tête : « Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated », suivi de la liste des clauses modifiées. Commit séparé `docs(specs): add memory model v0.1 corrective candidate`. La reconstruction suit la v0.1.
Contrats locaux : HandlePool v0.5 (Q3, Q4, Q5, Q12) et DS-v2 (Q11, Q27, Q28), changements listés dans la description de PR.
Preuves : refaire celles qui sont touchées ; les garanties de Q1, Q3, Q7 et B#45 sont démontrées sur les états atteignables du contrat, sans hypothèse supplémentaire non normative ; tout échec de preuve est rapporté, jamais contourné. Ouvrir la PR si la condition du brief est remplie.
</pasted_content id="c845">

```

**How to apply:** start a new pass from the latest branch tip; run an adversarial review workflow over module and report before delivering; `lake` is not on PATH, call `~/.elan/bin/lake`; keep the Lake library name `Ern`. `formal/Ern/.gitkeep` keeps showing as deleted: restore it with `git checkout`, never commit the deletion. A post-commit hook can make `git commit` exceed 2 minutes: give it a long timeout. The axiom rule ({propext, Quot.sound} only) forbids core lemmas that pull `Classical.choice` (`List.getElem?_mapIdx`, `List.eq_nil_iff_forall_not_mem`, `List.nodup_range`, `List.pairwise_lt_range`): sweep `#print axioms` over every theorem and replace them with local lemmas. Mathlib tactics (`set`, `tauto`) are unavailable. Reviews keep catching report errors: quote old forms from the old commit, count declarations with a command, and base an evidence claim only on a check that would fail on the defect. After fixing review findings, run a second targeted review of the fixes: in MM-03 pass 2 a fix over-rejected legitimate programs. Before calling a clause "missing" from an arbitrage, re-read every earlier arbitrage still in force: in pass 3 the clause needed for exitFrame_no_dangling was A4's root-holder rule, which A1 puts in WF3 and pass 2 had left out. `timeout` does not exist on this Mac: run `lake build` directly (about 2.5 min). When an arbitrage enlarges a definition used in hypotheses (pass 4: `Inv3` gained `NoDangling`), theorems whose text is unchanged silently narrow: give them only the conjunct they use. Before retiring a counterexample whose witness breaks a new invariant clause, look for another witness: pass-4 review found one and flagged the weakening as major. Check obligations against the initial state: the base frame of `S3.init` owns no place, so an obligation about it can be vacuous on reached states. A review fix can itself pick a semantic reading (pass 5: the kind conjunct of `IsInternalFor` rejected a `newArena` that D3 leaves undecided): check every fix for verdicts it changes on cases the text is silent on. Module docstrings must cite the report's own numbering, not the review's decision numbers. Arbiter-supplied theorems can be false: check them on small reached states (owned storage, a parameter that is the ancestor of another) before trying a proof. Every factual claim in the report needs a module witness, or reviewers flag it; never say "blocked until X" without checking escape sequences such as ending the owner value. When a precondition gains clauses, lemmas taking it as a hypothesis narrow silently: name the old precondition (pass 7: `EnterPreBase`) and give the lemmas only what they use. A guard on one operation (G2 on `store`) is usually bypassable through another (a helper authority then `release`/`endUse`/`free`/exit): look for such bypasses before claiming a configuration is excluded. A new check on an operation with a defined failure (`issue` → `fail`) must not turn that failure into `reject`. Use one adversarial reviewer per arbitrage lens; each found distinct real issues in pass 7. When a restriction rejects an old counterexample, try to rebuild a witness that satisfies the new clause before restating it as a rejection (pass 8: a same-shape destination restored `transfer_not_inv3_preserving`). Drop hypotheses a proof does not use. When cases disappear because their state is no longer reached, replay their verdicts on a new reachable state and list the drops. Machine-check every changed verdict the report lists, including the old witnesses' rejected steps. Never state "only clause X fails" as `X → Pre` next to `¬ X`: that is vacuous; name the other clauses (pass 8: `TransferPreBase` with an iff) and state them. Run a second targeted check after fixing verification findings: in pass 8 it caught that vacuous form. `omega` proving a conjunction goal pulls `Classical.choice`: split the goal first. `meta` is a keyword in this Lean: never name a hypothesis `meta`. `set` (Mathlib) is unavailable: use `obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ : ∃ x, x = e := ⟨_, rfl⟩`. `if_pos`/`if_neg`/`ite_cond_eq_true` are deprecated: use `simp only [h, ↓reduceIte]`. When `S3.Usable.mono` is applied with `rfl` for `hP`, give `(s := …) (s' := …)` explicitly or it unifies the wrong way. Simulation theorems: never quantify obligations over all translations (vacuous); put them as per-step premises of the run with parameters fixed once, and give a concrete multi-step run as witness. A universal encoding obligation (`∀ addr, decode (enc addr) = addr`) is unsatisfiable by a finite computable decode: state it per value. `lake env lean` uses the last built olean: rebuild the module before a scratch file uses new declarations. Never use an unquoted heredoc for Lean or docstrings: backticks run as shell commands; use `<<'EOF'` and pass paths by environment variable. `example`s escape a `collectAxioms` sweep: rename them to theorems in a scratch copy to check their axioms. `awk length` counts bytes, not characters: count line length in Python. Each check round finds errors in the previous round's wording: when a sentence is fixed in a docstring, grep the report for the same claim; quote arbitrages exactly (L2 said "hypothèse des énoncés", not "hors langage"); classify every item a deliverable asks to classify instead of moving it aside; a summary must not present a hypothesis restated in a conclusion as a result. Count theorem constants with internal ones (`isInternal`) and say which count you give. A callee cannot move a value out of a parameter's footprint (`ActiveDerivedOutside` counts the parameter itself): build values to transfer as callee locals. Authority ids shift with every alloc/issue/split: check them with `#eval` of `prun` prefixes before writing a case. A literal invariant from the material can fail under the full kernel extension: keep the literal statement with counterexamples and prove the parts that hold, under their own names. A runner's fallback state must be unreachable (e.g. no frame) or a statement "the run's state is reached" is vacuous when the run fails; give a lemma deriving success from reachability. Projecting `.2` out of an existential passes the elaborator but fails in the kernel: use `obtain`. When `step_ok_of`-style lemmas time out at `whnf`, pass the contract `k` and statics explicitly. Jalon 3 took four check rounds (11/9/9/4 confirmed): each round's fixes need their own narrow check. The list `Sublist` notation `<+` is scoped: write `List.Sublist`; `List.take_add` pulls `Classical.choice`. `omit … in` goes before the docstring. A `def` in a `variable (k : K)` section takes `k` only if it uses it: check call sites. In a multi-line `{ st with … }`, put each field on its own line at one column. Theorems stated for registered arenas (`ar ∈ s.arenas`) do not carry over to library instances: never cite them for one. Before writing "the only effect of X is Y", look for a witness in the other direction (derivability: the missing guard also turned a `fail` into an `ok`).

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.
- §47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; a static ownership cycle made §57 false in the initial state.
- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

## Validation and Revision Procedure

This edition has been validated and acquires normative authority under the ERN Charter v0. Any subsequent semantic change must identify the clauses concerned, justify the change, and preserve the guarantees of the ERN Charter v0. Formal models and proofs are instruments for verifying this specification, not sources of additional rules. Behaviors not determined within its scope are explicitly identified.

## Scope

This specification defines:

- the safe-code contract;
- the abstract machine for allocations, bytes, and accesses;
- the second-class access discipline;
- footprints, authorities, dependencies, frames, and ownership;
- read, write, transfer, release, allocation, and pinning transitions;
- the normative contract of arenas as a reference library abstraction;
- the correspondence obligations between these mechanisms.

It does not define syntax, the complete concurrency model, control-flow conventions, the type system, or compiler lowering. The sequential model's scope does not waive the general guarantees of the Charter.

---

# I. Safe-Behavior Contract

The following contract applies to all safe code and all properly encapsulated abstractions, regardless of their concrete memory representation.

## 1. Definitions of Safe Behavior

**Safe operation:** An operation that imposes no unchecked safety obligation on its user whose violation could compromise the language's guarantees.

**Safe code:** Code that executes only safe operations and does not directly assume obligations specific to unsafe operations.

**Safe interface:** An interface whose every permitted use preserves the language's guarantees when its implementation is correct.

**Safe abstraction:** An abstraction exposing a safe interface; its implementation may use unsafe operations provided it fulfills all their obligations.

/-! ## Initialization history (§59) -/

/-- Operation `op` writes leaf `l` from state `s` (§59): `write3` or `writeShared` of a list
containing `l`, `store` into `l`, or a `transfer` of which `l` is a destination leaf
corresponding to a source leaf `Init` before the step. -/
def KernelOp.Writes (s : S3) (l : Nat) : KernelOp → Prop
  | .write _ ls => l ∈ ls
  | .writeShared _ ls => l ∈ ls
  | .store _ p => l = p
  | .transfer src dst => l ∈ footprint s.P dst ∧
      ∃ l' ∈ footprint s.P src, corr s.P src dst l' = some l ∧ s.I l' = .init
authority (no origin) whose footprint is the footprint of a root place containing that leaf. -/
def RootChain (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (a : Nat) (y : Authority) (l : Nat), s.A[a]? = some y → l ∈ y.footprint → isLeaf s.P l →
    ∃ x z r, (x = a ∨ x ∈ s.ancs a) ∧ s.A[x]? = some z ∧ z.origin = none ∧ RootPlace s.P r ∧
      partOf s.P l r ∧ ∀ l', l' ∈ z.footprint ↔ l' ∈ footprint s.P r

/-- `RootHeld` (§49.7, §40): every usable root place has an active root authority of own mode
`Modify`, with no origin, held by the owner of the place, whose footprint is the footprint of the
place. -/
def RootHeld (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ r, RootPlace s.P r → s.Usable r → ∃ (i : Nat) (z : Authority) (pr : Place),
    s.A[i]? = some z ∧ z.active = true ∧ z.origin = none ∧ z.mode = .modify ∧
    s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ z.holder = pr.owner ∧ ∀ l, l ∈ z.footprint ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P r

/-- Auxiliary converse of `RootHeld` (§40, §49.7), not a clause of `WF3`: an authority with no
origin is held by the owner of the root place of every leaf it covers. -/
def RootHeldConv (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Nat) (z : Authority) (l r : Nat), s.A[x]? = some z → z.origin = none → l ∈ z.footprint →
    RootPlace s.P r → partOf s.P l r → ∃ pr, s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ z.holder = pr.owner

/-! ## `WF3` (§49) -/

/-- `WF3(s)` (§49): one field per item of §49. Index order of parents and origins represents
acyclicity (§49, last paragraph). -/
structure WF3 (s : S3) : Prop where
  /-- §49.1: the stack is nonempty and duplicate-free, every frame below `nF`. -/

/-- `I2` (§51): the origin of a derived authority exists; the derived mode does not exceed the
origin's, the derived footprint is within the origin's, and the origin of an active derived
authority is valid, that is, active. -/
def I2 (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (b : Nat) (y : Authority) (a : Nat), s.A[b]? = some y → y.origin = some a →
    ∃ x : Authority, s.A[a]? = some x ∧ y.mode.le x.mode ∧ (∀ p ∈ y.footprint, p ∈ x.footprint) ∧
      (y.active = true → x.active = true)

/-- `I3` (§52): every anchor of a usable place is valid (active). -/
def I3 (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, s.Active x

/-- `I4` (§53, first sentence): no read of a region containing a `Moved` leaf is permitted. -/
def I4 (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) (l : Nat), l ∈ ls → s.I l = .moved →
  ¬ Read3Pre s a ls

/-- `I1 ∧ I2 ∧ I3 ∧ I4` (§57). -/
def Inv3base (s : S3) : Prop := I1 s ∧ I2 s ∧ I3 s ∧ I4 s

/-- `NoDangling` (§54): no active authority covers a leaf of an unusable place. -/
def NoDangling (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (j : Nat) (y : Authority), s.A[j]? = some y → y.active = true →
    ∀ q, ¬ s.Usable q → ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, l ∉ y.footprint

/-- `Inv3 = I1 ∧ I2 ∧ I3 ∧ I4 ∧ AnchorOrder ∧ NoDangling` (§57). -/
def Inv3 (s : S3) : Prop := Inv3base s ∧ AnchorOrder s ∧ NoDangling s

/-- `I5` (§57): every pinned leaf, statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (an active pinning
obligation, §74), belongs to a usable place. The quantifier ranges over the leaves of the state
(§40): `K.Pinned` on an index that is not a leaf of `s` is not constrained. A specialized
obligation of `K.Pinned`, not a conjunct of the main invariant (§57). -/
def I5 (k : K) (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ l, l < s.P.length → isLeaf s.P l → (k.Pinned l ∨ s.pin l = true) →
    ∃ q, s.Usable q ∧ l ∈ footprint s.P q

/-! ## `NoOrphan` (§54) -/

/-- One link of a `NoOrphan` chain (§54): `a` is active and structurally covers every leaf of the
place holding `b`. -/
def CoversHolder (s : S3) (a b : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[b]?) (fun z => match z.holder with
    | .place q => s.Active a ∧ ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, l ∈ s.afp a
    | .frame _ => False) False

/-- Consecutive elements of a list are related by `R` (§54, chains of `NoOrphan`). -/
def Linked (R : Nat → Nat → Prop) : List Nat → Prop
  | a :: b :: c => R a b ∧ Linked R (b :: c)
  | _ => True

/-- `NoOrphan` (§54): every active authority held by a place ends a finite, non-repeating chain of
authorities whose first link is active and held by a frame of the stack, each link covering the
whole place holding the next. -/
def NoOrphan (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Nat) (y : Authority) (q : Nat), s.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true → y.holder = .place q →
    ∃ (a₀ : Nat) (z : Authority) (f : Nat) (c : List Nat), s.A[a₀]? = some z ∧ z.active = true ∧
      z.holder = .frame f ∧ f ∈ s.F ∧ (a₀ :: c).Nodup ∧ (a₀ :: c).getLast? = some x ∧
      Linked (CoversHolder s) (a₀ :: c)

/-! ## Initial state (§47) -/

/-- Declared static storage (§47): each element is (parent, owning static, kind) with its
initial state, `true` for `Init` and `false` for `Uninit` (read on leaves only). -/
abbrev Statics := List ((Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) × Bool)

/-- Well-formed statics declaration (§47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; §49, last
paragraph: the ordering of identifiers represents this well-foundedness, and that of structural
parents): parents and owning statics are earlier statics, and a part has its parent's owning
static (§49.2). -/
def StaticsOK (statics : Statics) : Prop := ShapeOK 0 (statics.map (·.1))

/-- Decidability of `StaticsOK` (§47). -/

/-! ## `freeSlot` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1, HP5-3, HP5-6) -/

/-- The effect of an accepted `freeSlot` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1): the pool exists with the
administration right, the handle is valid, and the content conditions hold; the arrival state is
`freeSlotEff`, whose kernel state and resolutions are those of the departure state (no end-of-use
effect; §36, §58), and whose slot is free with its generation incremented. -/
theorem freeSlot_effect {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle}
    (hst : FreeSlotStep j h L (.ok L')) :
    ∃ pl sl, L.pools[j]? = some pl ∧ pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl ∧ AdminRight L.kern pl ∧
      HandleOK L.kern pl h ∧ FreeContentOK L pl sl.place ∧ L' = freeSlotEff L j pl h.slot sl ∧
      L'.kern = L.kern ∧ L'.res = L.res ∧
      L'.pools[j]? = some (setSlot pl h.slot ⟨sl.place, sl.gen + 1, false⟩) := by
  cases hst with
  | @ok pl sl hp hH hR hsl hc =>
    exact ⟨pl, sl, hp, hsl, hR, hH, hc, rfl, rfl, rfl, getElem?_set_eq' hp⟩

/-- After an accepted `freeSlot(h)`, the freed slot is free with generation `h.gen + 1`, and `h` is
stale: `resolve` of `h`, and `resolveMany` of any batch containing `h`, fail (HandlePool v0.5,
HP5-6; §89). -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_then_stale {k : K} {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle}
    (hst : FreeSlotStep j h L (.ok L')) :
    (∃ pl' sl', L'.pools[j]? = some pl' ∧ pl'.slots[h.slot]? = some sl' ∧ sl'.live = false ∧
      sl'.gen = h.gen + 1) ∧
    (∀ m o, ResolveStep j h m L' o → o = .fail) ∧
    (∀ hs m o, h ∈ hs → ResolveManyStep k j hs m L' o → o = .fail) := by
  cases hst with
  | @ok pl sl hp hH _ hsl _ =>
    have hp' := getElem?_set_eq' (x := setSlot pl h.slot ⟨sl.place, sl.gen + 1, false⟩) hp
    have hs' := getElem?_set_eq' (x := (⟨sl.place, sl.gen + 1, false⟩ : Slot)) hsl
    have hn : ¬ HandleOK (freeSlotEff L j pl h.slot sl).kern
        (setSlot pl h.slot ⟨sl.place, sl.gen + 1, false⟩) h := not_handleOK_free hs' rfl
    obtain ⟨-, -, ho⟩ := hH
    rw [hsl] at ho
    exact ⟨⟨_, _, hp', hs', rfl, by rw [ho.1]⟩, fun m => (pool_resolve_invalid_fails hp' hn).2,

/-- A write that sets only `Init` leaves is the identity on the kernel state (§67 effect, §41). -/
theorem write3Eff_of_init {s : S3} {ls : List Nat} (h : ∀ l ∈ ls, s.I l = .init) :
    write3Eff s ls = s := by
  have e : (fun p => if p ∈ ls then InitSt.init else s.I p) = s.I :=
    funext fun p => by
      by_cases hp : p ∈ ls
      · simp only [hp, ↓reduceIte]; exact (h p hp).symm
      · simp only [hp, ↓reduceIte]
  unfold write3Eff; rw [e]

/-- HandlePool v0.5, HP5-3 (mandatory proof (2) of arbitration Q3): the metadata update of
`freeSlot` (free state, generation) is realizable by an authorized write under the administration
right. On every library-reachable state, under `DDSound` (§80) and `StaticsOK` (§47), for every
pool with `AdminRight` (§36), the pool value `v` (the place holding `internal`) exists and the
kernel `write` (§67) of the leaves of `v` through the authority grounding `MetaRight` is accepted;
when the leaves of `v` are `Init`, its effect is the identity on the kernel state. §76.5 requires
`Init` leaves only when the pool is created: on a library-reachable state with `AdminRight`, a leaf
of `v` can be `Moved` (`Witness.meta_write_not_identity`), and the write then changes the kernel
state, while `freeSlot` leaves it unchanged (`freeSlot_effect`). -/
theorem freeSlot_meta_write {k : K} {statics : Statics} (hdd : DDSound k)
    (hst : StaticsOK statics) {L : PState} (hr : PReach k statics L) {pl : Pool}
    (hR : AdminRight L.kern pl) :
    ∃ v a, Arena.arenaValue L.kern pl.entry = some v ∧
      Write3Step a (footprint L.kern.P v) L.kern (.ok (write3Eff L.kern (footprint L.kern.P v))) ∧
      ((∀ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P v, L.kern.I l = .init) →
        write3Eff L.kern (footprint L.kern.P v) = L.kern) := by
  have hk := kernel_guarantee hdd hst L hr
  obtain ⟨⟨y, hy, ya⟩, hm⟩ := hR
  unfold Arena.MetaRight at hm
  cases hv : Arena.arenaValue L.kern pl.entry with
  | none => rw [hv] at hm; exact (hm : False).elim
  | some v =>
    rw [hv] at hm
    obtain ⟨a, -, hex, hall⟩ : HasRight L.kern .modify v := hm
    have hhold : y.holder = .place v := by
      simp only [Arena.arenaValue, Pool.entry, hy] at hv
      revert hv; cases y.holder <;> simp
    have hu : L.kern.Usable v := by
      have := hk.1.holders _ y hy ya; rw [hhold] at this; exact this
    exact ⟨v, a, rfl, Guarded.ok (write_of_right hk hu hex hall fun _ h => h), write3Eff_of_init⟩

    ∃ pl i sl, L.pools[j]? = some pl ∧ AdminRight L.kern pl ∧ AllocSlotStatic L.kern pl dst ∧

      L'.kern.I dst = .init ∧ (∀ l, l ≠ dst → L'.kern.I l = L.kern.I l) ∧
      L'.pools[j]? = some (setSlot pl i { sl with live := true }) ∧
      slotHandle pl i = some ⟨pl.id, i, sl.gen⟩ := by

    refine ⟨pl, i, sl, hp, hst.right, hst, hsl, hf, rfl,
      by show (write3Eff L.kern [dst]).I dst = .init; simp [write3Eff], fun l hl => ?_,
      getElem?_set_eq' hp, by simp [slotHandle, hsl]⟩
    show (write3Eff L.kern [dst]).I l = L.kern.I l
    simp [write3Eff, hl]

(`Access.reachable_kinv`) and `ArenaInv` of the entry (`lReach_inv`) hold there; by I3 the check
of §78.3 never rejects after an accepted `derive` (`resetNoDeps_of_derive`), so the derived
operation is the kernel sequence `derive` then `release` (`reset_iff_derive_release`). -/

/-!
# DataStack: a library administrative abstraction (contract DS-v2, non-normative)

A `DataStack` instance of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`. The spec does not define
its contract (Part XIV preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their
library abstractions and are not defined here"). The contract formalized here is the library
contract **DS-v2**, which is **not normative**: every definition below that encodes a DS-v2 item
says so. The normative clauses that constrain it are §36 (`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable
on the stack value; the abstraction adds no rights to the kernel), §38 and §46 (library state
separate from `S₃`), §47 (empty initial registry), §56 (guard over all registries of live
administrations) and §58 (outcomes).

DS-v2 is DS-v1 with six changes. DS-v1: marks carry the stack identity and a fresh mark
identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks; `rewind m` fails on a dead or foreign
mark, rejects if an active authority derived from `internal` covers a cell above `m`, otherwise
returns those cells to available and removes `m` and every mark above it; `push` and `grow` use the
derived `issue` of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`: its static checks, the availability `fail`, then
`split` of `internal` and `store` of the block); `grow` is in place only (same base, extension into
the space directly after the block, `fail` otherwise). DS2-1: `mark` requires the administrative
right of §36 (`AdminRight`), else `reject`. DS2-2: `grow` stores the new block authority into the
place that currently holds the block authority `b`. DS2-3: a dead stack (`internal` inactive)
invalidates its marks, so `rewind` of a mark of a dead stack is `fail`, checked with the dead or
foreign mark, before the right. DS2-4: "a cell above m" is every cell at a position `≥ m.top`.
DS2-5: `grow` with `extra = 0` is accepted, an in-place reissue of the same region. DS2-6: `rewind`
on a stack index that does not exist is `fail`, like an invalid mark (`mark`, `push` and `grow` on
a missing stack stay `reject`). Also part of DS-v2: `push` without room is `fail`; `grow` of a `b`
that is no block of the stack is `reject`; §76.5 applies to `newStack`; the dead or foreign mark is
checked before the right of §36; §36 applies to `rewind`.

Every `ok` step of the library is a sequence of kernel steps O1–O16 (`DReach.reachable`), so the
abstraction adds no rights to the kernel (§36).

/-- Dynamic pinning depends only on the obligations (§74). -/
theorem S3.pin_congr {s s' : S3} (h : s'.pins = s.pins) : s'.pin = s.pin := by
  funext l; simp only [S3.pin, h]

/-- After `pin p`, a leaf is pinned when it was, or when it is a leaf of `p` (§74 `ok`
effect). -/
theorem pin_pinEff (s : S3) (p l : Nat) :
    (pinEff s p).pin l = (s.pin l || decide (l ∈ footprint s.P p)) := by
  simp [S3.pin, pinEff]

/-- Element `j` of `l.modify i f` (§75 `ok` effect), proved without classical reasoning. -/
private theorem getElem?_modify' {α : Type} (f : α → α) :
    ∀ (l : List α) (i j : Nat), (l.modify i f)[j]? = if i = j then (l[j]?).map f else l[j]?
  | [], i, j => by rw [List.modify_nil]; split <;> rfl
  | _ :: _, 0, 0 => rfl
  | _ :: _, 0, _ + 1 => by rw [List.modify_zero_cons]; split <;> first | rfl | (exfalso; omega)
  | _ :: _, _ + 1, 0 => rfl
  | _ :: l, i + 1, j + 1 => by
    rw [List.modify_succ_cons, List.getElem?_cons_succ, List.getElem?_cons_succ,
      getElem?_modify' f l i j]
    split <;> split <;> first | rfl | (exfalso; omega)

/-- The obligations after `unpin o`: obligation `o` is inactive, the others are unchanged (§75
`ok` effect). -/
theorem pins_unpinEff (s : S3) (o i : Nat) :
    (unpinEff s o).pins[i]? =
      if o = i then (s.pins[i]?).map fun ob => { ob with active := false } else s.pins[i]? :=
  getElem?_modify' _ s.pins o i

/-- After `unpin o`, a leaf is pinned exactly when an active obligation other than `o` covers it
(§75 `ok` effect: a leaf stays pinned while another active obligation covers it). -/
theorem pin_unpinEff_iff {s : S3} {o l : Nat} :
    (unpinEff s o).pin l = true ↔
      ∃ (i : Nat) (ob : PinOb), i ≠ o ∧ s.pins[i]? = some ob ∧ ob.active = true ∧
        l ∈ ob.leaves := by
  rw [S3.pin_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨i, ob, hi, ha, hl⟩
    rw [pins_unpinEff] at hi
    split at hi
    · cases h : s.pins[i]? with
      | none => rw [h] at hi; cases hi
      | some ob' => rw [h] at hi; cases hi; cases ha
    · exact ⟨i, ob, Ne.symm ‹_›, hi, ha, hl⟩
  · rintro ⟨i, ob, hne, hi, ha, hl⟩
    refine ⟨i, ob, ?_, ha, hl⟩
    rw [pins_unpinEff]; split

## HandlePool v0.5 = HandlePool v0.4 annex (Annex D of `~/Downloads/ERN_MM-03.3_v0.4_pour_validation.md`, lines 687–725) with these changes

- HP5-1 `freeSlot` (Q3). Preconditions: administration right (`AdminRight`: live pool, `MetaRight` =
  `Modify` exercisable on the pool value, §36); valid handle; no leaf of the entry is `Init` (each is
  `Uninit` or `Moved`); no active authority derived from a companion of this pool (a strict
  descendant of a companion recorded for this pool) covers a leaf of the entry. Effect: the slot
  becomes free and its generation is incremented; NO end-of-use effect: the kernel state is unchanged.
  Outcome order: keep the existing order of `FreeSlotStep` (`reject` without pool or right, then `fail`
  on an invalid handle, then `reject` on the content conditions); Q5 concerns resolution (§89) and is
  not extended to `freeSlot` (report this as a point for the user).
  Remove what only served the v0.4 `freeSlot`: `Exempt`, `DyingAccessOK`, `ContentAnchorOK`,
  `ContentEndPre`, `contentEnd_*`, `freeSlot_preserves*` on `endUseEff`, `freeSlot_lands_in_reachable`

  authority (kernel `write`), `transfer` of the entry's value to a local of the same shape, `unresolve`,

  storage root and stored in the pool value). The transfer relies on the v0.1 §63.4 exemption (the
  entry, the companion, `internal` and its origins ground the right). "Local": prefer a place created
  by `enterFrame` (§72) owned by the current frame; if that is infeasible in the run, use a static
  `Uninit` place directly owned by frame 0 and say why in the docstring and report.
- HP5-3 Mandatory proof (2) (Q3): the metadata update of `freeSlot` (free state, generation) is
  realizable by an authorized write under the administration right: for every library-reachable state
  and pool with `AdminRight`, the kernel `write` (§67, `Write3Pre`) of the leaves of the pool value
  (the place holding `internal`) is accepted. If the effect of that write is the identity on the
  kernel state (the pool value's leaves are `Init`, §76.5), state it too.

## DataStack DS-v2 = DS-v1 with these changes

DS-v1 (brief): "Marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list
of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from
internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every
mark above it; push and grow use the derived issue; grow is in place only (same base, extension into

rule), §63.9 (Q1), §71.2 (Q24), §74 and §75 (B#45), §76.6 (Q2), §78.3 (Q7), §82.2 (Q18), §86 (Q6).

**HandlePool v0.5** = HandlePool v0.4 annex D with:
- HP5-1 (Q3): `freeSlot` marks the entry free and increments its generation; no `endUse` effect, the kernel
  state is unchanged. Preconditions: administration right (live pool, `MetaRight`, §36), valid handle, no leaf
  of the entry `Init`.
- HP5-1' (Q3, second follow-up): no active strict descendant of this pool's `internal` covers the entry
  (replaces "derived from a companion"; covers §73 reanchoring onto `internal`). A pool nested in an entry
  blocks freeing that entry; the parent pool's authorities do not block the nested pool's `freeSlot`.

  stale); then `reject` without the right; then `reject` on the content condition.

- HP5-4 (Q4): D.2, D.3 and D.4 (3) per pool (the slot's pool); nested pools allowed.
- HP5-5 (Q5): handle validation precedes the right check in `resolve` and `resolveMany`: `fail`.
- HP5-6 (Q12): a handle of a free entry is stale: `fail`.
- HP5-7 (Q4): every library step is, on the kernel side, a sequence of accepted kernel steps O1–O16; the
  kernel guarantees hold on the whole state (`kernel_guarantee`).

**DS-v2** = DS-v1 with:
- DS2-1 (Q11 d): `mark` requires `AdminRight`, else `reject`.

J'ai ouvert la PR : [ernlang/ern#2](https://github.com/ernlang/ern/pull/2). La condition du brief est remplie : toutes les obligations sont prouvées et il ne reste aucun écart entre verdict attendu et verdict obtenu.

## État par question

La session précédente s'était arrêtée pendant l'audit final, avant la PR. Presque tout était déjà fait ; voici ce que j'ai vérifié dans le code.

| Q | État | Où |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | fait | §63.9 (`dstUsableAfter`) ; `reachable_kinv` sous `DDSound` et `StaticsOK` seuls ; le cycle de la v0 est rejeté (`reachable_cycle_rejected`) |
| Q2 | fait | §76.6 mixte, sur l'état d'arrivée ; porté par `NewArenaBase` |
| Q3 | fait | freeSlot v0.5 ; preuve (1) `freeSlot_after_transfer`, avec `internal` dérivé et un local créé par `enterFrame` ; preuve (2) `freeSlot_meta_write` |
| Q4, Q5, Q12 | fait | garanties par pool ; `fail` avant le contrôle du droit, aussi pour freeSlot ; handle d'une entrée libre périmé : `fail` |
| Q6, Q8, Q13–Q16, Q18, Q24 | fait | spec v0.1 et définitions qui citent ces clauses |
| Q7 | fait | `resetNoDeps_of_noCover` (§78.2 et I3) et `reset_iff_derive_release` (équivalence dans les deux sens) |
| Q9/Q26 | fait | I2 « origine active », §60.1, règle unifiée d'endUse et de free (`keptDesc`) |
| Q10, Q17, Q25, Q27 | fait | lectures retenues ; Q17 remplacée par l'exemption de la suite de Q3 |
| Q11, Q28 | fait | DS-v2 (DS2-1 à DS2-6) |
| Q19–Q22 | fait | jumeau H31a ; cas classés ; tableau des verdicts dans la PR ; `exitRoots` retenu |
| Q23 | **complété dans cette session** | B#45 n'avait aucun témoin sur un état atteignable. J'ai ajouté le cas `Corpus.MM3H.B45` (`d7cb2b7`) : pin(S), pin(f1), unpin de f1, puis transfer(f1, d). Le transfer est rejeté ; le jumeau sans pin(S) est accepté. |

## Vérifications refaites

- `lake build` : 28 jobs, aucun avertissement.
- Le grep des tokens interdits ne trouve rien.
- `collectAxioms` sur les 25 modules (6396 constantes) : rien en dehors de `propext` et `Quot.sound`.

## Points ouverts, listés dans la PR, non bloquants

1. **Spec v0.1** : la phrase de la v0 « This edition has been validated… » a été recopiée telle quelle et contredit l'en-tête. Elle n'est pas dans la liste des amendements, donc je ne l'ai pas modifiée.
2. **Preuve (2) de Q3** : si une feuille de la valeur du pool est `Moved`, l'écriture qui réalise freeSlot la rend `Init`, alors que freeSlot ne change pas l'état du noyau.
3. **W2** : avec l'exemption du §63.4, le cas ne peut plus exprimer le déplacement d'une ligne par un autre acteur pendant la vue.
4. **H49** : la règle de suite de Q9 rend `reject` les endUse 2 et 3, qui étaient `ok` dans la base historique de Q21.
5. **DS2-4** : la lecture retenue n'est pas plus stricte que l'alternative B de DS-R1 ; les deux sont incomparables.
6. **MM23-H16** : la règle de l'adresse la plus basse reste une décision du brief, pas une règle de la spec.

Je n'ai pas relancé l'audit final à plusieurs agents qui avait été interrompu. Les revues adverses faites à chaque phase, mes propres vérifications et la revue Codex de la PR le remplacent. La PR n'a pas de CI pour l'instant, et l'auto-fix est actif.
